BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION                             )
OF EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR                              )
REVISION OF ITS RETAIL ELECTRIC                              )       Docket No. 25-00082-UT
RATES PURSUANT TO ADVICE NOTICE                              )
NO. 317                          )
                                 )

                                       COMPLETENESS REPORT

          Pursuant to the Hearing Examiner’s July 16, 2026, Sua Sponte Order Vacating Procedural

Schedule, Tolling Pending Deadlines, and Requiring the Filing of an Amended Application (“Sua

Sponte Order”), the Public Interest Advocacy Staff (“Staff”) of the New Mexico Public Regulation

Commission (the “Commission”) respectfully files the following Completeness Report. This filing

follows Staff’s review of El Paso Electric Company’s Amended Application for Revision of Retail

Electric Rates (“Amended Application”) dated August 6, 2026. In short, based on Staff’s review

of the Amended Application to date, the filing appears to be sufficiently complete to allow this

litigation to proceed. Staff would show the Hearing Examiners the following:

                                                  Background

          1.       After EPE filed a second errata to its application in this docket on July 7, 2026,1

and a number of intervenors submitted a joint objection in response,2 the Hearing Examiner issued

the Sua Sponte Order directing the Company to file a new Amended Application “and a complete

replacement filing package.”3 The evident intent of this directive was to ensure that EPE had

 brought forth “a single, complete, internally consistent, and reviewable presentation of [its] …

proposed rates.”4

           2.    The Sua Sponte Order also specifically directed Staff to review EPE’s Amended

Application upon filing. Staff was ordered to file “a Completeness Report” stating “whether the

Amended Application and supporting materials are sufficiently complete, coherent, internally

consistent, and technically usable to permit the proceeding to continue.”5

           3.    As part of this Completeness Report, the Sua Sponte Order outlined ten non-

exhaustive criteria for Staff to consider:

                 1) EPE filed all materials required by this Order;

                 2) the Amended Application identifies one authoritative and operative
                 version of EPE’s case;

                 3) the correction and reconciliation matrix is complete and usable;

                 4) all identified corrections appear to have been carried through affected
                 materials;

                 5) the amended cost-of-service study and associated models are complete
                 and executable;

                 6) the amended testimony, schedules, workpapers, proposed tariffs, and rate
                 calculations are internally consistent;

                 7) Staff can trace material adjustments and requested amounts through the
                 filing;

                 8) the Amended Application resolves the facial inconsistencies and
                 omissions identified in the pending motions and objections;

                 9) EPE has adequately supplemented affected discovery responses; and

                    10) additional foundational corrections or supplementation appear
                   necessary before Staff and intervenors can fairly prepare testimony.6

One of these criteria, number 9, was later withdrawn by order of the Hearing Examiners.7

          4.       Staff’s Completeness Report of EPE’s Amended Application was subject to strict

parameters as ordered by the Sua Sponte Order. In particular, the review was to be limited to

“procedural completeness, coherence, internal consistency, and usability.”8 By contrast, Staff was

directed not to “provide any advice or commentary” on matters properly subject to litigation and

substantive dispute among the parties, namely “whether EPE’s substantive requests are reasonable,

lawful, or supported by the weight of the evidence.”9

          5.       As directed by the Sua Sponte Order, Staff has concluded its Completeness Report

of EPE’s Amended Application.

          6.       This Completeness Report does not express Staff’s view of the substantive requests

in EPE’s Amended Application or whether any requests therein are reasonable, lawful, or

supported by the weight of the evidence. Staff also expresses no opinion in this report as to

whether, standing alone, EPE’s testimony and supporting exhibits are sufficient to carry the

Company’s burden of proof on any issue in dispute in this administrative litigation. Staff’s analysis

and conclusions are strictly limited to the parameters outlined by the Hearing Examiners in the

Sua Sponte Order.

             7.     Staff understands the intention of the Sua Sponte Order was not necessarily to

create a “perfect” application free of minor errors, particularly in a proceeding of this size.10 Staff’s

review focused on the substance of the Amended Application with the understanding that the

purpose of the Sua Sponte Order was to create a complete and consolidated filing that the parties

could rely on in the development of the case.

                                                Analysis

            8.     Having reviewed EPE’s Amended Application, Staff concludes that, as a general

matter, it is “sufficiently complete, coherent, internally consistent, and technically usable to permit

the proceeding to continue.”11 Although Staff has identified several minor errors over the course

of its review (see #11 below), these issues do not appear to represent the sort of “material omissions

and errors” that would prevent the adjudication of this case.12

            9.     As directed by the Sua Sponte Order, EPE’s Amended Application package refiled

each of the Company’s testimonies, exhibits, work papers, and other supporting documents. The

Amended Application itself also clearly states that it represents the singular and exclusive version

of the Company’s case.13 EPE filed what appears to Staff to be a complete and usable correction

and reconciliation matrix, and the corrections necessitated by the two errata appear to have been

carried through all affected materials. The amended cost-of-service study and associated models

appear to be complete and executable. For the most part (see #11 below), the amended filing is




10

 internally consistent. Staff has found that it is able to trace material adjustments and requested

amounts throughout the filing.

           10.     Staff has also considered the Hearing Examiner’s criterion that the Amended

Application should resolve “the facial inconsistencies and omissions identified in the pending

motions and objections.”14 Many of these alleged inconsistencies, as best Staff could determine,

pertained to the impact of the second errata on EPE’s revenue requirement. These have now been

resolved through the Company’s more comprehensive update of its supporting documents and

testimonies. Other alleged inconsistencies and omissions, however, have not been resolved

because they do not relate to completeness of the Amended Application and instead are substantive

issues in dispute. For example, the City of Las Cruces has argued that EPE has failed to comply

with 17.1.3 NMAC by not providing explanations or linkage data for a future test year rate filing.15

Notwithstanding this alleged missing material, EPE disputes the City’s characterization of its filing

and therefore the issue itself should be addressed through motions practice.16 As another example,

while parties may well challenge (successfully or otherwise) EPE’s new advertising invoices by

arguing that EPE has effectively done “nothing more than dump[…] more invoices into the

 record,”17 under 17.3.350.9 NMAC this appears to represent a question of whether EPE has carried

(or will carry) its burden and not whether the Amended Application itself is legally complete.18

           11.       Nevertheless, Staff’s review has identified several areas that should be brought to

the attention of the Hearing Examiners, some of which may require additional analysis.19 These

issues include:

                     A.     Advice Notice: EPE complied with its responsibility to carry through all

corrections throughout its filings20 but has not sought to file a new advice notice. This means that,

while the correction to the revenue requirement and rate calculations are evident throughout the

Amended Application and the new tariffs, the same is not true for the suspended advice notice.

This is explained as follows by the (amended) Direct Testimony of George Novela:

           EPE is not requesting to file a new advice notice with the proposed rates in the
           Amended Filing. The change in the Amended Filing is not material; it amounts to
           only 0.04% of the originally filed revenue requirement. At any rate, EPE accepts
           that the Commission cannot order rates higher than what were publicly noticed in
           Advice Notice No. 317.21

Staff understands this to mean that EPE is not seeking to recover the increase to the revenue

requirement caused by the second errata and is instead requesting approval of the noticed rates and

revenue requirement included in Advice Notice No. 317.


17
     Expedited Joint Objection, at 10.
18
   See 17.3.350.9(D) NMAC (providing, as the “burden of proof,” that a utility “seeking to include any
advertising expenditures in determining its cost of service must affirmatively show through the presentation of
clear and convincing evidence that each expenditure is allowable”).
19
   “Staff may state that particular matters require additional discovery or substantive analysis without treating
those matters as completeness defects, provided the operative filing and supporting information are sufficiently
clear and complete to permit that discovery or analysis to proceed.” Sua Sponte Order, at 14. Staff would also
note that, on Friday, August 7, 2026, it became aware that the Excel file version of EPE’s Schedule A-01
distributed to the parties was not fully executable (in that some of the numbers were hard-coded). Staff alerted
EPE to this error, and it was immediately rectified.
20
     See id. at 8, 14.

                 B.      Rule 440 Package: Although each document within this package has its own

unique cover letter identifying the applicable project, the associated Rule 17.5.440 Form provided

by EPE for each project contains the same (identical) information concerning the Talavera

Distribution Substation. This appears to have been an inadvertent technological error, as this

mistake was not made in the Rule 440 package accompanying the original application.

                C.      Rate 09: There appears to be an error in EPE’s rate design workpaper for

Rate 09, as the rate itself is designed to establish an on-peak period between 3:00 P.M. to 7:00

P.M. (MST), Monday through Friday, during the summer months. The workpaper, however, uses

five (5) peak hours. This is an error, but in Staff’s view it represents a drafter’s mistake rather than

the type of substantive inconsistency that would render the application itself unable to be litigated.

                D.      Victor Martinez Testimony: Mr. Martinez’s testimony contains outdated

information concerning two projects. Mr. Martinez’s testimony states that the two projects are

“expected” to enter service on dates that have now since passed. In Staff’s view, this is not

significant and can be further clarified through discovery if parties deem necessary.

                E.      Jennifer Nelson Testimony: Ms. Nelson’s testimony contains minor

changes not listed in EPE’s matrix. The minor changes can be understood in context or by analysis

of the tracked changes identified in Ms. Nelson’s amended Direct Testimony. Staff does not

believe that these minor, untracked changes result in the Amended Application being incomplete

and further believes that parties could seek more information through discovery if parties find the

untracked changes difficult to follow.

                                             Conclusion

        Staff has undertaken a good faith effort to review EPE’s Amended Application, as directed

by the Sua Sponte Order, and finds that it is sufficiently complete to allow this matter to proceed.

 This is not to say that Staff necessarily agrees (or disagrees) with any particular component of

EPE’s Amended Application, but only that, as Staff has thus far ascertained, the Company has

filed a complete application sufficient for and capable of litigation through the administrative

adversarial process.

                                                   Respectfully submitted,
